abilities.name: lightning-rod
abilities.effect: Redirects single-target electric moves to this Pokémon where possible.  Absorbs Electric moves, raising Special Attack one stage.

kanto.flavorText: In the autumn spawning season, they can be seen swimming powerfully up rivers and creeks.

original-johto.flavorText: When autumn comes, the males patrol the area around their nests in order to protect their offspring.

hoenn.flavorText: It punches holes in boulders on stream­ beds. This is a clever innovation that prevents its eggs from being attacked or washed away by the current.

original-sinnoh.flavorText: To protect its family, it will fight with its drill-sharp horn. It lives in hollowed rocks in streams.

extended-sinnoh.flavorText: In autumn, its body becomes more fatty in preparing to propose to a mate. It takes on beautiful colors.

updated-johto.flavorText: Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.

original-unova.flavorText: In autumn, its body becomes more fatty in preparing to propose to a mate. It takes on beautiful colors.

updated-unova.flavorText: In autumn, its body becomes more fatty in preparing to propose to a mate. It takes on beautiful colors.

kalos.flavorText: It makes its nest by hollowing out boulders in streams with its horn. It defends its eggs with its life.

updated-hoenn.flavorText: Seaking is very protective of its eggs. The male and female will take turns patrolling around their nest and eggs. The guarding of eggs by these Pokémon goes on for over a month.

original-alola.flavorText: Trainers who are crazy for Seaking are divided into horn enthusiasts and fin enthusiasts. The two groups do not get along well.

updated-alola.flavorText: To attract females, males dance on the river’s floor. The females gather around the male that dances most gracefully.

letsgo-kanto.flavorText: It is the male’s job to make a nest by carving out boulders in a stream using the horn on its head.

swsh.flavorText: Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.
